title: Add tests for QueryLogs store method
description: Add unit tests for the new QueryLogs method covering: filtering by method, path, status, limit, minutes, and combinations of filters.

title: Add query parameters to ListLogs store method
description: Extend the LogStore interface and SQLite implementation to support filtered log queries. Add a LogQuery struct with fields: Method (string), Path (string), Limit (int), MinutesAgo (int, optional). Update ListLogs to accept LogQuery and build a WHERE clause filtering by method, path, and timestamp (using MinutesAgo to compute a cutoff). Keep backward compatibility with the existing ListLogs(limit) usage by making all filter fields optional (zero values = no filter).

title: Pass nonce through auth flow into id_token
Support implicit flow (response_type=token id_token) at auth endpoint
description: Houston/APC sends response_type=token id_token (implicit flow). oauth-tester currently only supports authorization_code flow and always returns a code. Need to detect implicit flow response_type and return tokens directly in the redirect URI fragment.

title: Authorization & Token Flow
description: Implement the authorization endpoint (login page with username/password form) and token endpoint (exchanges auth code for JWT). This is the core OIDC authentication flow.

title: Authorization endpoint with login page (GET /auth)
description: Implement GET /auth endpoint. This is the authorization endpoint in the OIDC flow. It must: 1) Accept query params: client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, scope, state. 2) Render a minimal HTML login form with username and password fields and a Login button. 3) On form submission (POST /auth), validate username/password against users in SQLite (plaintext comparison). 4) On success, generate a random authorization code, store it in SQLite (mapped to the authenticated user and redirect_uri), and redirect to redirect_uri?code={code}&state={state}. 5) On failure, re-render the login page with an error message. Auth codes should expire after a short TTL (e.g. 5 minutes).

title: Token endpoint (POST /token)
description: Implement POST /token endpoint. Accepts form-encoded body with: grant_type=authorization_code, code (the auth code from /auth), redirect_uri, client_id. Must: 1) Look up the auth code in SQLite, validate it hasn't expired and redirect_uri matches. 2) Delete the auth code after use (one-time use). 3) Generate a signed JWT ID token with claims: iss (ISSUER_URL), sub (username), aud (client_id), exp, iat, email, name. Sign with RS256 using the in-memory private key. Include kid in JWT header. 4) Return JSON response: {access_token, token_type: bearer, id_token, expires_in}. The access_token can be the same as the id_token for simplicity.

title: Machine-Readable Log Query API
description: Add a filtered, machine-readable log query endpoint so that LLM agents (and humans with curl/jq) can fetch OIDC exchange logs programmatically. The existing GET /api/logs returns all logs (up to 200) with no filtering. We need query parameters for: HTTP method, path, result count (limit), and optionally a time window (minutes ago). Response format should be minified JSON for LLM-friendliness. The existing DELETE /api/logs (clear logs) endpoint already exists and is usable as-is.

title: Add DELETE /api/logs to clear logs (verify existing)
description: Verify that the existing DELETE /api/logs endpoint works correctly for programmatic use (no UI/confirm dialog needed). This endpoint already exists and returns 204 on success. Just confirm it works via curl and document it. No code changes expected unless issues are found.

title: SQLite Storage Layer
description: All state stored in SQLite via modernc.org/sqlite (pure Go, no CGO). Schema includes users table (username, password, email, name) and request_log table (timestamp, method, path, request_headers, request_body, response_status, response_headers, response_body). Database file created on startup if missing. Architect for future SCIM support.

title: SQLite schema and database initialization
description: Create SQLite database on startup using modernc.org/sqlite. Define schema: users table (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, username TEXT UNIQUE, password TEXT, email TEXT, name TEXT), request_log table (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, timestamp DATETIME, method TEXT, path TEXT, query TEXT, request_headers TEXT, request_body TEXT, response_status INTEGER, response_headers TEXT, response_body TEXT), auth_codes table (code TEXT PRIMARY KEY, username TEXT, redirect_uri TEXT, scope TEXT, created_at DATETIME). Run migrations on startup. Passwords stored as plaintext. Architect the storage layer as an interface so SCIM tables can be added later.

title: User CRUD data access layer
description: Implement Go functions for user CRUD operations against SQLite: CreateUser, GetUser, UpdateUser, DeleteUser, ListUsers. These are used by both the web UI and the auth endpoint. Keep as a clean interface/struct that the HTTP handlers call.
close_reason: Already implemented in store.go during schema task

title: Request/response logging middleware and data access
description: Implement HTTP middleware that captures requests and responses for OIDC endpoints only (/.well-known/openid-configuration, /jwks, /auth, /token). Log method, path, headers, body for requests and status, headers, body for responses. Write to the request_log table in SQLite. Also implement ListLogs and ClearLogs data access functions for the logs UI page. Do NOT log /ui/* or /api/* requests to avoid noise.

title: Add response status filter to log query API
description: Add a 'status' query parameter to GET /api/logs that filters by HTTP response status code. Examples: ?status=400 (exact match), or consider supporting prefix matching like ?status=4xx for all 4xx errors. This helps diagnose failures quickly — e.g. 'show me all failed requests' without knowing which endpoint failed. Must be added to both the LogQuery struct in the store layer and the HTTP handler's query param parsing.

title: Add GET /api/logs query parameter support to handler
description: Update the ListLogs HTTP handler to parse query parameters from the request URL: method (HTTP verb, e.g. POST), path (endpoint path, e.g. /token), limit (number of results, default 50), minutes (time window in minutes, optional). Pass these to the updated store method. Return minified JSON (no indentation). Example: GET /api/logs?method=POST&path=/token&limit=3 returns the 3 most recent POST /token exchanges.

title: Use client_id from auth request instead of env var for audience claim
OIDC Discovery & Cryptographic Keys
description: Implement in-memory RSA key generation, JWKS endpoint, and OIDC discovery document. These are the foundational OIDC endpoints that the enterprise product queries to learn about the IdP.

title: In-memory RSA key pair generation
description: Generate an RSA key pair (2048-bit) on startup. Store in memory only. The private key is used for signing JWTs, the public key is exposed via JWKS. Generate a stable key ID (kid) for the key. Use crypto/rsa and crypto/rand from stdlib. Key is regenerated each time the process starts (no persistence).

title: JWKS endpoint (GET /jwks)
description: Implement GET /jwks endpoint that returns the public key in JWKS (JSON Web Key Set) format. Must include: kty=RSA, use=sig, alg=RS256, kid (matching the key ID used in JWT headers), n (modulus, base64url), e (exponent, base64url). Response Content-Type: application/json.

title: OIDC Discovery endpoint (GET /.well-known/openid-configuration)
description: Implement GET /.well-known/openid-configuration returning a JSON discovery document. Required fields: issuer (ISSUER_URL), authorization_endpoint ({ISSUER_URL}/auth), token_endpoint ({ISSUER_URL}/token), jwks_uri ({ISSUER_URL}/jwks), response_types_supported ([code]), subject_types_supported ([public]), id_token_signing_alg_values_supported ([RS256]), scopes_supported ([openid, email, profile]), grant_types_supported ([authorization_code]). Content-Type: application/json.

title: Web UI
description: Web UI served from the same Go binary. Three UI concerns: (1) Login page at /auth for OIDC flow — standard IdP login form. (2) User management page at /ui/users — editable grid for CRUD on users, updates SQLite on each cell edit. (3) Logs page at /ui/logs — displays every HTTP request and response so the user can see OIDC flow at the protocol level. All HTML served via Go templates or embedded files.

title: User management grid page (GET /ui/users)
description: Web page at /ui/users showing all users in an editable grid/table. Each row shows username, password, email, name. Support: add new user row, delete user, inline edit of any cell. On edit, immediately update SQLite (via AJAX/fetch calls to JSON API at /api/users). Simple HTML + minimal JS, served from Go templates or embedded files. Include shared nav bar linking to Users and Logs pages.
close_reason: Already implemented in ui.go during previous task

title: Logs viewer page (GET /ui/logs)
description: Web page at /ui/logs that displays every HTTP request and response logged by the middleware (OIDC endpoints only). Show timestamp, method, path, request headers/body, response status/headers/body. Auto-refresh or polling to show new entries. Crucial for understanding the OIDC flow at the HTTP level. Simple HTML + minimal JS. Include shared nav bar linking to Users and Logs pages.

title: User management JSON API endpoints
description: REST API for the user management UI: GET /api/users (list all), POST /api/users (create), PUT /api/users/{id} (update), DELETE /api/users/{id} (delete). Returns JSON. Called by the user management grid page via fetch.

title: Support client_secret validation on token endpoint
description: Houston sends client_secret when using authorization code flow. oauth-tester needs to accept (and optionally validate) the client_secret on POST /token.

title: Project Scaffolding & Configuration
description: Project initialization, Go module setup, HTTP server with TLS on port 443, and configuration (issuer URL, client ID, TLS cert paths). Single static binary.

title: Initialize Go module and project structure
description: Run go mod init, create main.go entry point, and establish the package structure. Add modernc.org/sqlite as dependency. Package layout: internal/store (SQLite storage layer), internal/oidc (OIDC endpoints and logic), internal/crypto (key generation and JWT), internal/ui (web UI handlers and templates). Architect so SCIM can be added later as internal/scim.

title: Implement HTTP server with routing
description: Set up net/http server with TLS (cert.pem/key.pem) listening on port 443. Route to OIDC endpoints: GET /.well-known/openid-configuration, GET /jwks, GET /auth, POST /auth, POST /token. Route to web UI pages: GET / (redirect to /ui/users or landing page), GET /ui/users, GET /ui/logs. Route to JSON API: /api/users. All /ui/* pages share a nav bar linking to Users and Logs. Use standard library only. Logging middleware is a separate task.

title: Server configuration (TLS, port, issuer URL, client ID)
description: Parse configuration from environment variables. Required: ISSUER_URL (the external URL of this IdP including scheme, e.g. https://oauth-tester.example.com — used in discovery doc and JWT issuer claim), CLIENT_ID (the client ID that APC will use). TLS cert/key default to cert.pem and key.pem in CWD. Server listens on port 443. SQLite database is hardcoded to oauth-tester.db in CWD. Env vars only, no CLI flags.

title: User configuration via environment variables
description: Support multiple users configured via environment variable. Suggested format: USERS env var containing JSON array, e.g. [{"username":"alice","password":"pass123","email":"alice@example.com","name":"Alice Smith"}]. Each user needs: username (for login), password (for login), email (JWT claim), name/display name (JWT claim). The sub claim in the JWT can be derived from username. All user data lives in RAM only.
close_reason: Users now managed via web UI + SQLite, not env vars

title: Add groups claim to id_token for Houston claimsMapping
